_doc: T-240: the rideable horse (gravelight/world/horse/horse.gd; the pure rules in horse_rules.gd, tested by test_horse_gait.gd). Loaded by HorseRules.table() (not a GLData table). Placement is per map: <map>.json "horses" rows {name, pos [x, y, z] (where the horse stands tied), yaw (degrees, the way it faces: 0 = north / -Z), rail [x, y, z] + rail_yaw (the hitching rail; omit for none), zones [the zone ids it may stand in], look}. ride: speeds are m/s at the walk, the trot and the gallop; pace is 0 stand .. 3 gallop and moves by urge_per_s while forward is held (sprint_urge_per_s with sprint), ease_per_s with no input (it comes back toward a walk on its own), rein_per_s while back is held; back held at a stand backs it up at back_speed. accel / decel / brake are m/s^2. turn_rate is radians per second at a stand / walk / trot / gallop (a turning circle of speed / rate: 6 m at the gallop's turn_gallop_speed, which a hard turn brings the gallop down to); turn_lag_s is how long the turn takes to answer (an animal, not a car). eye is the rider's eye over the saddle's seat; look_free the radians either side of the horse's nose the rider may look. mount_s / dismount_s the climbs up and down; hold_s the Use hold for either. fire: the rider may shoot at a stand, a walk and a trot (the gait's own motion is the sway, times sway_walk / sway_trot) and not at a gallop (both hands are on the reins). crowd: zombies within radius count; each one past free takes pace_per off the fastest pace it will go (never under min_pace), and at shy_at of them it shies (a snort, the pose). trample: at speed_min or faster, a zombie within radius of its chest is flung aside (push m/s for push_s), takes damage and costs the horse slow of its speed; at most one every cooldown s. boss_fear: a horse boss within radius: it will not go faster than max_pace and whinnies. home: left alone for idle_s it walks back to its rail (pace) and stands as it was tied; it gives up for retry_s if it cannot get on. bounds: it may stand only in its zones (those open), within y_up / y_down of its rail's height.
